Empirical Research Plan  
“Do publicly–released corruption audits hurt incumbent mayors, and is the effect
stronger where local media are present?”

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Identification Strategy
Strategy:  Random-assignment difference-in-differences (DID) / randomised
experiment.  

•  The CGU lottery assigns municipalities to be audited in month t.  
•  Whether the audit report is released before or after the Oct-2004 election is
therefore as-good-as-random, conditional on the audit calendar.  
•  We compare the change in incumbents’ electoral performance from the previous
election (2000) to 2004 between (i) municipalities whose reports were released
before the vote (treated) and (ii) municipalities audited later (control).  
•  Because corruption severity is measured only for audited places, we use a
“difference-in-difference-in-differences” (DDD): the interaction of
(i) Early audit × (ii) Corruption severity.  
•  Randomisation justifies causal inference; DID absorbs time-invariant
municipal characteristics and common election-cycle shocks.

Why not RDD/IV?  The timing threshold is calendar-time, not a running variable;
and assignment is already random, so no instrument is required.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. Treatment and Control

•  Treatment indicator  Early_i  = 1 if municipality i’s CGU audit report was
released ≥30 days before the 03 Oct 2004 election (exact cut-off can be varied
±15 days in robustness); 0 otherwise.  

•  Control group: municipalities drawn in the lotteries but whose reports were
released only after election day (including those audited after 03 Oct or whose
reports were delayed). Because all of them were randomly drawn, they provide a
valid counterfactual.  

•  Treatment timing: event date is 03 Oct 2004. Pre-period=2000 election,
post-period=2004 election.  

•  Continuous “dose”:  Corrupt_i  = number (or log number) of infractions
flagged by auditors, normalised by total items inspected.  

•  Media moderator  Media_i  = number of AM radio stations in 1999 (or dummy for
≥1).  We will test interaction  Early × Corrupt × Media.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. Key Identifying Assumptions

A1.  Random audit timing: conditional on qualifying for the lottery,
whether the report came out before vs. after Oct-2004 is random.  
• Plausibility: the draw is televised, balls are drawn simultaneously, no
observable lobbying. Timing differences arise only from draw date and clerical
delays.

A2.  Parallel trends: in absence of early disclosure, incumbents in early and
late‐audited municipalities would have experienced the same change in vote
share from 2000→2004.  
• Plausibility: previous election outcomes (2000) are balanced by design; we
will test pre-trend equality using earlier elections (1996 vote shares) for a
subset.

A3.  Stable Unit Treatment Value (SUTVA): audit disclosure in municipality i
does not directly affect voting in j ≠ i.  
• Plausibility: local mayoral races are highly localised; media coverage is
largely municipal. We will drop multi-city media markets as robustness.

A4.  No differential attrition: all audited municipalities appear in the TSE
data.  
• Plausibility: turnout is compulsory; any missingness is administrative and
testable.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. Threats to Identification & Remedies

T1. Report-production lags correlated with municipal capacity.  
   Remedy: control for pre-existing state capacity proxies (fiscal revenue per
   capita, paved-road ratio); show balance; instrument actual “report
   released” with lottery order (first-month-draw dummy).

T2. Spill-overs via regional radio/newspapers.  
   Remedy: drop municipalities sharing the same media market with treated units;
   or cluster standard errors at media-market × state; run spatial
   HAC (Conley) standard errors.

T3. Incumbent selection/retirement differences.  
   Remedy: restrict sample to municipalities where the 2000 incumbent seeks
   re-election (about 75 %); control for term-limit status; show balanced
   re-running propensities across groups.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. R Code Outline (executable)

```r
# 0. Packages
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)
library(lmtest)
library(sandwich)

# 1. Load data ----------------------------------------------------------
elec   <- fread("tse_municipal_2000_2004.csv")       # election outcomes
audit  <- fread("cgu_audits_2003_2005.csv")          # audit dates + infractions
census <- fread("ibge_census_2000.csv")              # socioeconomic covars
media  <- fread("ibge_media_1999.csv")               # AM radios etc.

# 2. Merge & construct --------------------------------------------------
dat <- merge(elec, audit, by = "muni_id")
dat <- merge(dat, census, by = "muni_id")
dat <- merge(dat, media,  by = "muni_id")

# Treatment: report released ≥30 days pre-election
election_day <- as.Date("2004-10-03")
dat[, report_date := as.Date(report_date)]
dat[, early  := as.integer(report_date <= (election_day - 30))]

# Outcome: change in incumbent vote share (ΔVS)
dat[, inc_share_2000 := vote_share_2000[incumbent==1], by=muni_id]
dat[, inc_share_2004 := vote_share_2004[incumbent==1], by=muni_id]
dat <- unique(dat, by="muni_id")
dat[, d_vs := inc_share_2004 - inc_share_2000]

# Corruption intensity
dat[, corrupt := infractions_total / items_examined]

# Media
dat[, radio_dummy := as.integer(am_radios >= 1)]

# 3. Main specification -------------------------------------------------
fe_formula <- d_vs ~ early*corrupt + X_popden + X_income + X_urban +
                          factor(state_id)

model_main <- feols(fe_formula,
                    data = dat,
                    cluster = ~ state_id)

etable(model_main)

# 4. Media heterogeneity -----------------------------------------------
model_media <- feols(d_vs ~ early*corrupt*radio_dummy + X_popden + X_income +
                     factor(state_id),
                     data = dat, cluster = ~state_id)
etable(model_media)

# 5. Robustness: instrument early with draw_before_apr_2004 ------------
dat[, early_iv := as.integer(draw_month <= "2004-04")]
iv_main <- feols(d_vs ~ 1 | early ~ early_iv + corrupt + controls,
                 data=dat, cluster=~state_id)
etable(iv_main)

# 6. Placebo: use municipalities audited 2002 (pre-program) ------------
# Assuming a dataset 'audit2002' exists
placebo <- feols(d_vs ~ early*corrupt, data=audit2002, cluster=~state_id)
summary(placebo)
```

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. Expected Results

Theory: Voters punish malfeasance if they learn about it. Therefore:

•  Early × Corrupt coefficient < 0.  
•  Magnitude: a 1 s.d. increase in revealed corruption (≈0.15 of items) is
expected to lower incumbent vote share by ~5 percentage points, reducing
re-election probability by 10 pp.  

•  Triple interaction with media: negative effect roughly doubles where ≥1 AM
radio station is present.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (DID)

C1. Random/parallel trends supported by pre-trend test ………………… 1  
C2. No anticipation of audits before lottery………………………………………… 1  
C3. No differential attrition/missing outcomes…………………………………… 1  
C4. No spill-overs between treatment & control………………………………… 0.5  
C5. Correct functional form & robust SEs……………………………………… 1  

Total = 4.5 / 5 ‑- strong but must monitor spatial spill-overs.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
End of plan
